insights: The residue count is the index of the squares subgroup: |residues| = |(ZMod p)ˣ| / |ker(squaring)| = (p−1)/2 by the first isomorphism theorem in cardinality form.
The kernel has exactly 2 elements because the only square roots of unity in a field are ±1, distinct precisely when p is odd; the hypothesis 2 < p enters only through one_ne_neg_one_units.
Counting is cleanest in the unit group (where squaring is a homomorphism); unitsEquivNeZero transports |range| to the count of nonzero field squares without recomputation.
Independent of the parent's analytic route (Euler's criterion +1-values): both compute the same index-2 subgroup of squares.
The method generalizes to k-th power residues: u ↦ u^k has kernel of size gcd(k, p−1).

# Knowledge Base: euler-criterion-squares-oq-01-oq-01

## Problem
Count the nonzero quadratic residues of an odd prime p: exactly (p−1)/2.

## Approach (COMPLETE)
Structural, via the squaring homomorphism sqHom : (ZMod p)ˣ →* (ZMod p)ˣ, u ↦ u².
- Kernel = {1, −1}, cardinality 2 (distinct because p odd).
- First isomorphism theorem ⇒ |image| = |(ZMod p)ˣ| / |kernel| = (p−1)/2.
- isSquare_coe_iff_mem_range identifies the image with the nonzero field squares.
- Nat.card_congr + unitsEquivNeZero + subtypeSubtypeEquivSubtypeInter transport the count.

Result: card_nonzero_quadratic_residues, 8 theorems / 1 def, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide. Confirmed at p = 7 (3 residues).

## Dead Ends
None — the kernel/image route compiled directly.
